scope: Source-only prompt tests using the built-in image generation tool; not a FLUX benchmark or local iPad runtime

tests.name: eye
tests.inputRole: Source eye only; example stencil withheld
tests.prompt: Use case: style-transfer edit. Input image 1 is the ONLY source and edit target: a realistic drawing of one eye. Convert this SAME eye into a professional tattoo transfer stencil. This is a fidelity test, not a redesign. Preserve the source's framing, aspect ratio, eye angle, canthi positions, eyelid shapes, iris position and diameter, visible pupil/catchlight silhouette, and the directions and grouping of the visible lashes. Keep the eye at the same scale and placement within the original canvas. Render only clean opaque black strokes on a pure white background. Use deliberate, thin, smooth continuous curves for the upper and lower eyelid rims, the visible iris boundary, pupil/catchlight boundary, and the important visible upper and lower lashes. The pupil should be an unfilled outlined shape, not a solid black mass. Select only a few source-supported short iris detail marks; omit the dense iris texture. Retain a few necessary crease/form guides as sparse short dashed black strokes, clearly less dense than structural outlines. Remove all grayscale shading, paper grain, skin texture, sketch noise, crosshatching, solid black shaded patches, signature and lettering. Do not simply threshold the photograph or trace every tonal edge. Do not add decorative elements, invent anatomy, redraw a generic eye, regularize the lashes into an even fan, enlarge the iris, or move any feature. Output one stencil of the original eye only, on the same landscape white canvas, with no labels, comparison layout, borders or extra images.

tests.name: masked-portrait
tests.inputRole: Source art photo only; no target stencil or generated eye included
tests.prompt: Use case: style-transfer edit. The single input image is the original artwork and the ONLY visual source. Convert that exact tall tattoo composition into a professional tattoo transfer stencil, keeping the same portrait framing and all existing design elements in their original positions. Preserve the woman's facial proportions, expression, gaze, both visible eyes with their eyelid/iris/pupil boundaries, nose, lips, jaw, visible finger positions, fingernails, rings, flowing hair, crown/graffiti shapes, curved crossing graphic strips and banknote stacks. Do not redesign or beautify the face or invent extra fingers or symbols. Use clean, thin, deliberate continuous BLACK contour lines on pure WHITE. Major object overlaps and facial anatomy must be readable; avoid multiple redundant wavy outlines. Do not fill shadow regions with solid black. Simplify the hair to long directional groups, jewelry to the important silhouettes and selected details, and banknotes to outlines and a few identifying internal marks. Use sparse short dashed black guides only for the most necessary broad facial and hand shading transitions. Omit skin texture, pores, photographic grain, all dense hatchwork and all grayscale shading. Ignore the photographed screen's glare, moire and dirt/physical blemishes; they are not the artwork. Keep the existing crown and partially visible WARNING lettering as supported by the original; no new text, signature, watermarks, captions or decorative frame. Do not mirror, recrop, reposition elements, change proportions, change the composition, or replace the subject with a generic woman. Produce a single clean stencil on a tall white canvas matching the source aspect ratio, with no before-after panels. Favor source fidelity and a sparse useful transfer map over decorative illustration.
